SMTO-MAN-0001 — SMTO has no entry for this error code

GUID: 49ac8455-32f2-4315-8fef-c383161211f4
Slug: catalog-reference-not-found
Domain: MAN · Subsystem: man

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to explain an error code, but this installation has no entry under that code. The code may be mistyped, or it may come from a different SMTO version.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Compare the code with the original message one character at a time. SMTO error codes look like SMTO-MAN-0001: SMTO, a dash, letters, a dash, four digits. The lookup only matches an exact code, so one wrong character makes it fail.
  2. Reload the page, then open the error again and select Explain this error. A page left open while SMTO was updated can ask for codes that the running server's error list doesn't have.
  3. Open Manual and type the error code into the Search manual box. Errors this version knows normally have their own Manual page, so the search shows whether the code exists here.

What success looks like

  • The error's explanation opens with a title and How to fix steps.

If it still fails

  • Copy the error code and note where you saw it, then send both to the person who manages SMTO; they can check whether it comes from a newer or older SMTO version. Don't edit any SMTO files to add the code.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The error catalog lookup endpoint (GET /api/agent/errors/ followed by the reference) returned 404 because error_exists() found no Error ID, GUID, slug or alias matching the supplied reference in the installed error catalog.

What this means

  • The catalog lookup endpoint calls error_exists on the supplied reference and finds no registered identity or alias in this installed catalog. Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.

Why this can happen

  • The catalog lookup endpoint calls error_exists on the supplied reference and finds no registered identity or alias in this installed catalog.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact ID/GUID/slug/alias with the installed version and avoid guessing similar identifiers.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the exact reference (Error ID, GUID, slug or registered alias) against GET /api/agent/errors/catalog. If the reference came from a different SMTO build, for example a page left open across an update, align the page and Server versions; the installed catalog is static and needs no repair.
  • Check the exact Error ID, GUID, slug or registered alias and the installed product version.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A registered reference resolves to its immutable catalog entry.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
